scores.note: Good idea for an opening spread, ruined by a skeletal foreground chair, a 2.06 m dollhouse camera height, 25% dead sky and a right subwoofer that is entirely behind the panel.
The hero conditioner is effectively invisible. Two 23%-wide diagram slabs and 14 labels own the frame; the left loudspeaker is a clipped, equally-bright distraction.
One card wall covering 55% x 60% of the stage, six plot regions on it, hero clipped by the bottom frame edge, two label kickers chopped by the card border.
The hardware crop is the best in the deck; the framing wastes it. Card touches the top frame edge, seven graphs, and the monoblock's lit meter outranks the subject.
The only real hero shot: proper three-quarter, clean diagonal, readable silhouette. Held back by two labels occluded by the tonearm and by unbacked outline diagrams that break the house language.
No identifiable hero. Overlay traces run across the rack faceplates and bleed off the left frame edge straight through the chapter rail. The least legible frame in the set.
The hero rack is bisected by the explanation panel — a knob is cut in half at the panel edge. Competent 2x2 card grid, wrong subject in the centre of frame.
Card abuts the panel with no gutter, panel eq text clips mid-glyph, six curve fragments run off the left edge through the rail, and the rear panel floats detached above the rack.
Camera aimed at the rack, not the monoblock. The subject is a 210 px object at the left frame edge with eight nav items and a label printed on top of it.
Worst frame. The 1.25 m floorstander is chopped into two disconnected pieces by an overlay slab and buried under a wireframe box, three cards and eight free traces.
Hero subwoofer is ~4% of frame; the left one is hidden behind the turntable. Mid-frame is a knot of overlapping traces, and the chair reappears clipped at the bottom.
As a closing spread it is the busiest frame in the piece. Four cards, eleven labels, no focal point, two kickers overprinting each other, and labels running under the panel.
System reads and the rack silhouette works, but every cabinet is a flat value with no clearcoat gradient, the floor mirrors nothing, and the tweeter carries a blown white square.
The conditioner — the subject — is completely occluded by two black diagram planes. 50% of the frame is below 5% luminance. There is almost no render left to judge.
44% of the frame is under 2% luminance behind one enormous black card. The hardware that survives is decent but rainbow-fringed by the CA pass and rim-glowing on every edge.
Best-lit rack stage; the fascia, display and knobs are legible. Ruined by rack posts clipping to white with bloom halos and by the diagram card ghosting the preamp display through it.
The one frame with a genuine product-photography moment — the platter rim arc. Undone by a dead-matte record with no groove sheen and no label, and blown square blobs on the dust cover.
The rack has become a neon wireframe: roughly thirty uniform white edge lines, all equally bright, several on downward-facing edges. Traces cut straight through the chassis.
Left third is empty grey backdrop, the hero component is half behind the text panel, the monoblock meter is a pale decal. Same edge-glow problem as phono.
Card ghosting is worst here — rack shelves and a blown post streak are clearly visible through the graph plate, which destroys both the diagram and the object.

The stage is called Monoblocks and the monoblock is at the extreme left edge, cropped and dim, while the camera frames the rack behind a translucent card. No heatsink detail survives; the fins are a black void.
The motor cutaway is untextured grey and pale-blue boxes with blotchy noise — the exact 'grey plastic box' the brief bans, and the worst material in the piece.
A flat desaturated teal wash covers the lower half of the frame with a hard straight seam at its far edge. The sub cone carries four hard white squares that read as stuck-on LEDs.
Bloom fog is out of control: a blown square on the right speaker's midrange throws a halo that washes out a quarter of the frame. Contrast is gone.

The best label system in the piece: every caption sits directly above the graph card it names, left-aligned to its edge. Loses points for the clock-edge caption disappearing under the toroid and for the panel slicing an .eq in half.
Good card-caption discipline, but the top caption crowds the masthead at y=43 and the Δ-Σ caption is printed over the graph above it.
Clean top band, and the one stage with a visible leader line that works (OUTER GROOVE). 'BELT DRIVE' floats 200px from the belt with nothing joining them.
The rack callouts read as a stacked legend, not annotation. Two labels land on the chapter rail. The THE GAIN eq is the finest single piece of typesetting in the project.
Five of nine labels sit on top of live graph traces; SEALED CHAMBER swings between the rail and fully off-screen.
NODES · MODE (1,1,0) destroys two rail rows; the myth callout is 4px above the panel fold, i.e. invisible.
.eq clips 'worst case, at 105 k[Hz]' at the panel edge — visible truncation. Two labels share a baseline and read as one run-on line.
Pole/zero labels scattered below the plot with no leaders to the markers; 'CHASSIS EARTH' and 'CARRIERS OSCILLATE' share a baseline; the myth block prints '3.5×1016'.
The LINE PREAMP label is destroyed by a bright cyan sine passing through the glyph bodies — the single worst legibility failure in the set.
Fourteen labels; four on the rail; 'Supply' overlaps 'Neutral · back'; 533 prose words against a 320 ceiling.
Worst rail collision in the piece, an orphaned 'THE METER' h3 alone at the panel edge, two whole sections below the fold, five broken readout bars.
Four rail collisions including an amber value printed over the active chapter pill, plus an illegible three-label pile-up on the rack's specular highlight.

verdicts.lens: THE DIGITAL CHAIN — streamer + dac (loudspeaker engineer / measurement editor)
THE ELECTRICAL CHAIN — power, preamp, xover, amp, and the electrical claims in overview
The mechanical and acoustic chain — turntable, phono, speaker, sub, air (loudspeaker engineer / measurement editor)

findings.what: Every stage is composed for the full canvas, but src/app.css permanently reserves the right and left edges: #panel is right:24px, width min(31.5vw,436px) (so CSS x 1140-1576 at a 1600 px viewport) and #chapters plus #masthead occupy x 0-140. The genuinely readable stage is CSS x 156-1124, y 96-930 — a 968 x 834 box, aspect 1.16, whose centre is at 41% of frame width, NDC x = -0.18. No stage's shot{} is aimed at that centre; they are all aimed at NDC 0.
findings.fix: Add a shared SAFE constant (e.g. in src/core/layout.js next to SHOTS: SAFE = {l:0.098, r:0.703, t:0.096, b:0.930} as fractions of viewport) and re-aim every shot{} so the subject's projected centroid lands at NDC x = -0.18, y = +0.05, and so the subject's projected bounding box fits inside SAFE with a 6% margin. Practically: for the six rack stages shift target.x by about +0.18 m (toward +X) or move camera.x left by a similar amount so the rack lands in the left 60% of the canvas. Verify by re-shooting and checking the subject's silhouette does not cross device x = 2280 (panel) or x = 280 (rail).
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: The hero is bisected by the explanation panel. src/stages/preamp.js:686 shot is position [0.910, 1.466, -0.459] target [-0.28, 1.06, -2.90]; because the camera sits at x = +0.91 and looks toward x = -0.28, the rack at x = 0 projects into the right third of frame and runs under #panel. At full res the preamp's right-hand knob is sliced in half by the panel edge at device x = 2280, and every shelf's right end is cut.
findings.fix: Change preamp.js:686 to something like position [0.62, 1.34, -0.30], target [0.16, 0.94, -2.92], fov 30. Aiming target.x at +0.16 (right of the rack) swings the rack into the left-of-centre band. Re-shoot and confirm the rightmost rack geometry ends before device x = 2200, leaving an 80 px gutter to the panel.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: The 1.25 m loudspeaker does not read as one object. In shots/speaker.png the head unit (tweeter + midrange) sits isolated at upper-left, separated from the bass cabinet below by the bright horizontal plane of the motor-cutaway card; they read as two unrelated boxes. The baffle is additionally covered by a translucent cyan wireframe box, which destroys the single continuous specular running the height of the cabinet that is the whole Wilson signature.
findings.fix: Two changes in src/stages/speaker.js. (1) SHOT at :754 is [1.35,1.16,0.74] -> [-0.32,0.70,-2.49] fov 36 — a chest-height wide. A 1.25 m object needs a portrait treatment: drop to position [1.05, 0.86, 0.30], target [-1.40, 0.70, -2.45], fov 30, so the cabinet fills ~80% of the SAFE box height and the camera is below its midpoint. (2) Move the whole motor/cutaway overlay group to +X of the cabinet so nothing crosses the baffle, and delete the cyan bounding wireframe over the front face entirely — the cabinet's own edge highlight must be unbroken from plinth to top cap.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: The camera is pointed at the wrong object. src/stages/amp.js:781 shot targets [-0.122, 0.625, -2.78] — that is the equipment rack at x = 0, not a monoblock (LAYOUT.monoL/monoR are at x = -0.95 / +0.95). The result: the rack is the 400 px centre-of-frame object, while the actual monoblock is a 210 px shape jammed against the left frame edge with the chapter rail printed across it, and the second monoblock is entirely behind the panel.
findings.fix: Retarget amp.js:781 onto the left monoblock as a single hero: position [-0.05, 0.78, -1.72], target [-1.02, 0.52, -3.02], fov 32. That puts the monoblock in the left-of-centre band at roughly two-thirds frame height, with the rack falling away as a soft background mass at right. Move the schematic card to the right of the monoblock, in the space the rack currently wastes.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: src/core/labels.js promises a depth test in its docstring ("with a depth test so it hides behind geometry when it should"), stores opts.hideBehind at line 42, and constructs this._raycaster at line 19 — but update() never reads either. Labels therefore print through solid geometry. This is the single root cause of the label-on-hardware failures in dac ("ANALOGUE | DIGITAL" bisected by a chrome shelf highlight), turntable ("INNER GROOVE", "STYLUS" cut by the tonearm pillar), amp ("LOAD / Bl 12 N/A" bisected by a rack post) and phono ("T1 POLE 3180 us" over the rack column). update() also has no exclusion for the panel or rail regions and no label-vs-label resolution — it only culls at +/-140 px outside the canvas.
findings.fix: In labels.js update(), after projecting: (a) raycast from camera through the label's world anchor and fade the label to ~0.15 opacity if the first hit is nearer than the anchor by more than 2 cm and item.hideBehind is true; (b) hard-cull (opacity 0) when the projected x lands inside the panel rect (x > w - 470) or the rail rect (x < 155 and |y - h/2| < 210) or the masthead rect (x < 320 and y < 92); (c) run one greedy pass over the visible items measuring getBoundingClientRect and nudging the later label's offset[1] by +/-18 px until no two rects intersect. This is a core file — flag it to the owner rather than patching stage code around it.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: Direct text-on-text collision. The "METER / log · 30 dB to 300 W / 98 W mean" label sits at roughly device x 85-300, y 928-1024, exactly on top of the chapter-rail entries "04 Turntable" and "05 Phono stage". The glyphs interleave; neither string is readable. Additionally the active rail item "08 Monoblocks" is printed directly on the monoblock's front face above the blue meter, and "07 Crossover" and "09 Loudspeaker" sit on the chassis.
findings.fix: Once the amp camera is retargeted (see the amp framing finding), move the METER label's anchor to the monoblock's right-hand side with offset [+90, -10] so it never enters x < 320. Independently, the rail exclusion in labels.js must guarantee this class of collision cannot recur in any stage.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: Four or five disconnected overlay curve fragments run off the LEFT frame edge (device x 0-600, y 280-1070) with no card behind them and no label attached. They pass straight through chapter-rail items 00-05, so cyan traces cross the nav typography. It reads as rendering garbage, not as a diagram. The stage also has no identifiable hero: I cannot tell which box in the rack is the phono stage.
findings.fix: In src/stages/phono.js, clamp the RIAA trace group's world extent so nothing projects left of NDC x = -0.80, and give it a DIAG.diagramCard backing plate so the curves sit on a plate rather than floating over the room. Separately, single out the hero: give bay 3 a brighter key or a subtle rim, pull the camera in (phono.js:681 fov 34 -> 28, target y 0.755 -> 0.70) so the phono chassis is at least 30% of the SAFE box width.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: Same left-edge bleed as phono: six curve fragments (cyan and orange) clipped by the left frame edge at device x 0-530, y 470-1450, printing over rail items 05 through 11. "11 Air & ear" is completely buried under a cyan sine. Additionally the label "ACTIVE CROSSOVER 1 IN 3 / 80 Hz / 2.20 kHz" sits on the active "07 Crossover" pill.
findings.fix: In src/stages/xover.js, delete the left-hand ghost traces entirely (they carry no labelled information in the still) or move that group to +X of the rack. Move the ACTIVE CROSSOVER label anchor to the rear-panel slab with offset [+70, 0].
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: The hero has been swamped. The mains conditioner in rack bay 0 is not findable in shots/power.png — it is behind and below two diagram slabs each about 23% of frame width and 45% of frame height, which together consume ~45% of the stage. Those slabs carry eight separate plot regions (three copper-bar panels, a lattice inset, four stacked graphs), and power.js makes 14 labels.add calls against the contract's stated ceiling of ~10. The left loudspeaker, clipped at the frame edge, is the same tonal value and roughly the same size as the whole hero region.
findings.fix: In src/stages/power.js: keep the right-hand card (the four mains-cycle graphs) and cut the left slab to one panel — the live/neutral pair with the drift-vs-field ratio — dropping the lattice inset and the third bar. Cut labels from 14 to 8 by folding the lattice, true-ratio and mains-lead callouts into content(). Then reframe power.js:992 from fov 27.5 at position [2.02,1.44,2.65] to roughly position [1.35,1.10,1.35], target [0.10,0.62,-2.90], fov 30, so the conditioner chassis is the largest single object in the SAFE box and the surviving card sits beside it, not over it.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: The listening chair is the foreground hero of the opening spread and it reads as flat-pack garden furniture. Built at src/stages/overview.js:107-230 and placed at :538-541 at LAYOUT.listener, it is the nearest object to the camera, so it takes the strongest vignette and the strongest chromatic aberration; the key light does not reach it, so the leather goes to pure black and only the chrome sled and posts survive — the object reads as a skeleton of tubes. It has no floor contact shadow, so it floats. It is clipped by both the bottom and left frame edges, and the TIME SCALE slider and transport buttons are drawn on top of it.
findings.fix: Do not cut it — a chair back-to-camera in the near foreground is the right editorial device for a room spread — but rebuild the staging. (1) Add GEO.contactShadow(0.86, 0.72) under it at overview.js:541. (2) Add a low, dim fill from camera-left (a small rect area or point at about [3.4, 1.5, 4.6], intensity low, colour matched to the room's key) so the leather channels read as leather and the object becomes a lit silhouette with a rim rather than a wire frame. (3) Move it to LAYOUT.listener.x - 0.55 and rotate ~0.10 rad so it reads as a corner-anchored crop rather than a centred obstruction, and so it clears the transport chrome above y = H-120.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: The right subwoofer is entirely behind the explanation panel, so the system is asymmetric in the one frame whose job is to show the whole system. Arithmetic: shot at overview.js:527 is position [2.48,2.06,6.80], target [0.17,0.75,-2.55], fov 28.5; at the sub plane (z = -3.28, ~10.1 m away) the half-width of the frustum is 10.1·tan(14.25°) = 2.56 m, and LAYOUT.subR.x is 2.92 — outside it, and the right 29% of what remains is covered by the panel anyway. The left sub survives only as an amber glow behind the turntable plinth.
findings.fix: Either (a) widen to fov 34 and retarget to [-0.35, 0.72, -2.55] so both subs land inside the SAFE box, or (b) commit to the tighter frame and deliberately let both subs bleed symmetrically off the left and right of the SAFE box as dark bookends — which requires shifting target.x to about -0.45 so the composition is symmetric about the SAFE centre rather than about the canvas centre. Option (b) is the stronger picture; option (a) is the honest system diagram. Pick one, do not leave it asymmetric.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: Camera height reads as a dollhouse. overview.js:527 puts the eye at y = 2.06 m looking down at a system whose tallest element is 1.25 m, so every speaker is seen from above and none of them tower. Combined with the target at y = 0.75, the hardware compresses into a horizontal band from ~37% to ~64% of frame height, leaving a dead black band across the top 18% and a dead floor across the bottom 20%.
findings.fix: Drop to seated ear height: position [2.10, 1.22, 6.40], target [-0.35, 0.82, -2.55], fov 32. That lifts the speakers against the cyclorama, kills the top dead band by letting the cabinets reach into it, and gives the classic reference-room look. Re-check the chair does not then fill the lower third — if it does, pull it further left per the chair finding.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: The diagram card touches the top frame edge (device y ~30) so there is zero sky, and it carries seven graph regions — reconstruction sinc sum, zero-order hold, 20 kHz sampled sine, amplitude floor, aperture/images, 1-bit stream, shaped-noise FFT. dac.js declares 7 DIAG.Graph instances. A magazine spread does not put seven plots on one page. The hero DAC is a 440 x 70 px strip two-thirds down the frame while the card owns the top 60%.
findings.fix: In src/stages/dac.js, cut to three graphs on one card: the sinc sum (the argument), the zero-order hold with the filter removing it (the myth), and the shaped-noise FFT (the number). Move the aperture, 1-bit stream, amplitude-floor and 20 kHz panels into content() as prose plus one eq block. Then pull the card down and left so its top edge sits at device y >= 130 and reframe dac.js:557 to fov 26 with target [0.06, 0.72, -2.94] so the DAC chassis, not the card, is the largest element.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: The monoblock at bottom-left is the brightest, highest-contrast object in the frame — a lit blue meter on a chromed chassis — and it is not the subject. It is clipped at the left frame edge and sits directly under chapter-rail items 09/10/11, which become illegible grey-on-light-metal. The same problem recurs in preamp (monoblock centre-bottom), phono (monoblock clipped at right) and speaker (monoblock at right).
findings.fix: Either reframe so the monoblock leaves the shot, or in each of those stages dim the off-subject monoblock's meterGlow emissive by ~70% when the stage is not 'amp'. The cheap version: in dac.js/preamp.js/phono.js/speaker.js set the camera so no lit meter falls inside the left 20% or the SAFE box's brightest quadrant. The subject must be the brightest thing in the frame; right now it never is.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: One diagram card spans device x 440-2200, y 96-1310 — 55% of stage width and 60% of its height, a wall in front of the room. It carries six plot regions. Its bottom edge chops two label kickers mid-height: "BUFFER · 0-140 MS · 300 MS WINDOW" and "SNR VS T_J · 0.1 PS-10 NS · 80-170 DB" are both half-cut by the card boundary. Below it the streamer chassis and the rack are clipped by the bottom frame edge.
findings.fix: In src/stages/streamer.js, split the wall: keep the packet-arrival histogram, the AES3 subframe strip and the clock-edge eye on one card sized to about 1.5x the streamer's own width, and drop the biphase square waves, the transmission-line block and the SNR-vs-jitter line into content(). Move both clipped labels inside the card bounds (or anchor them below it). Raise streamer.js:705 target.y from 0.755 to 0.82 and drop fov to 30 so the rack base is inside the frame.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: The OCXO callout — the gold-lidded oscillator module at device x 1825-2260, y 1440-1770 — floats free at an arbitrary tilt with no visible connection to the hardware, and its right corner abuts the panel with roughly a 20 px gutter. Its label "OCXO · 24.576 MHz · ±120 fs / island x2 · needs < 0.77 ps" is set in the dimmest grey over the gold lid and is effectively illegible.
findings.fix: Straighten it to a plane parallel to the stage camera, move it left so its right edge is at least 90 px clear of device x = 2280, and connect it to the streamer chassis with a DIAG leader line so it reads as a callout. Put the label above the module on the dark plate, not over the gold.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: As the closing frame of the piece this is the busiest image in the deck and has no focal point at all. Four diagram cards, eleven labels.add calls, roughly ten free traces, plus circles and arcs, all at 20% object scale in a wide room shot (air.js:231, position y = 2.15 m, fov 40). Two kickers overprint each other around device x 360-700, y 1040 ("WAVEFRONT · 200 HZ · λ..." and a "WEIGHT..." kicker). "FLOOR BOUNCE · IMAGE SOURCE 0.95 M DOWN / +0.400 m of path" is chopped by the cochlea card's border. The "AT THE SEAT ... 100 W" label at device x 1920-2260 runs into the panel. The chair reappears at bottom-centre with only its backrest showing, clipped by the frame.
findings.fix: Rebuild this as a resolution image, not a summary. Pick one idea — the ear, or the seat with the direct and floor-bounce paths — and stage it at hero scale. Cut to two cards maximum and six labels. Drop the camera to position [0.85, 1.25, 4.10], target [0.10, 1.02, -1.40], fov 34 so the listening position reads at human height. Remove the chair from this frame entirely (it is the overview's prop and only ever appears clipped here).
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: The hero is ~4% of the frame. SHOT at sub.js:211 is position [0.45, 3.55, 6.60], fov 44 — an almost plan view from 3.55 m. The right subwoofer renders as an 80 x 105 px box; the left one at LAYOUT.subL is completely occluded by the turntable and its plinth. Meanwhile device x 810-1490, y 600-980 is an unreadable knot of overlapping cyan and amber traces sitting on top of the rack, and the room-mode pressure map ends up as a soft blue blob in the bottom-right corner, mostly under the panel, reading as a lens flare rather than a pressure field.
findings.fix: Split the intent. Keep a moderately high camera for the modal floor pattern but drop to position [0.30, 2.35, 5.40], target [0.90, 0.42, -1.90], fov 38 so the right sub reads at a useful size and the floor plane still shows. Move the mode-pattern plane's bright lobe left, to about x = -0.6, so it lands inside the SAFE box instead of under the panel. Move or thin the trace knot over the rack — at this camera the rack is not the subject and should be a quiet mass. And remove the chair from this stage's frame (it appears clipped at the bottom and adds nothing).
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: The label "ROOM MODES · MODE (1,1,0) · 30.02 HZ / the seat sits on one" prints directly on top of chapter-rail items "08 Monoblocks" and "09 Loudspeaker" at device x 230-560, y 1130-1200. Text on text, both unreadable.
findings.fix: Anchor it to the floor-plane node line at about x = +0.4 with offset [+40, -12] so it lands well right of device x = 320. The rail exclusion in labels.js is the systemic fix.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: The .eq block in src/app.css:153 uses white-space:pre with overflow-x:auto. In a still render that silently clips. Confirmed on xover: the line "|LP| = |HP| = 0.5 at fc → 20·log10 0.5 = -6.02 dB" touches the eq border and the commentary "worst case, at 105 H" is sliced mid-glyph. The available measure is #panel width min(31.5vw,436px) minus 48 px scroll padding minus 26 px eq padding = 362 px, at 12.5 px JBMono with -0.012em tracking, i.e. about 52 characters.
findings.fix: Hard-cap every .eq line in every stage's content() to 52 characters, moving trailing commentary onto its own <span class="c"> line. Sweep all twelve stages — xover.js is the confirmed offender, and dac.js and phono.js have lines within a few characters of the limit.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: Panel body copy runs off the bottom of the frame mid-sentence in power ("— a further ×3000 on top of the"), xover ("oscillate ±92 nm about a fixed point. The field crosses the") and air. #panel is fixed top:24 bottom:24 with an internal scroll, which is correct behaviour in the app but means the still — the thing being judged as a magazine spread — always shows a truncated final line.
findings.fix: Add a bottom fade to #panel-scroll (a 40 px linear-gradient mask to transparent) so a cut line reads as intentional continuation rather than a broken layout, and trim the affected content() bodies toward the low end of the contract's 150-320 word range so the whole argument fits at 1000 CSS px height.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: The diagram language is inconsistent stage to stage, which breaks the piece as a series. power, streamer, dac, amp and speaker use solid black DIAG.diagramCard slabs with a hard rectangular edge against the room — they read like a poster taped over the photograph. turntable and xover use thin unbacked outline frames floating on the raw background. phono has graphs with no backing at all, so the rack shows through the plot and its gridlines beat against the rack's horizontal rails at nearly the same spacing.
findings.fix: Pick one treatment and apply it in all twelve: DIAG.diagramCard with reduced opacity (about 0.72) and a 12 px feathered edge rather than a hard rectangle, so it reads as a projected overlay rather than a pasted object. Give every graph a backing plate — phono.js is the file that currently has none. Standardise the card's size relative to its subject at 1.4x the component's projected width, per the contract's 1.2-2x guidance.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: Diagram density is roughly double what the format can carry. On-screen plot-region counts: dac 7, power 8, streamer 6, xover 7, speaker ~6, preamp 5, air 4 cards. Nothing in the frame tells the eye which one to read first, so the reader defaults to the panel and the 3D becomes wallpaper. Label counts also exceed the contract's stated ~10 ceiling: power 14, xover 13, air 11, phono 10, speaker 10.
findings.fix: Impose a hard budget and enforce it per stage: maximum three plot regions and maximum eight labels visible at once. Everything cut goes into content(), which is the right place for the third and fourth supporting number. Where a stage genuinely needs more, stage them with setReveal(k) so only one or two are up at any activation level rather than all of them simultaneously.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: Label collision at the top of frame: "MOTOR FORCE / F = Bl·i / -13.4 N" and "CHARGE CARRIERS / oscillate — they never arrive / ±5.2 µm · shown ×200" overlap horizontally around device y 420-520, with "-13.4 N" touching "oscillate". Separately "SEALED CHAMBER / 30 L net · Vas 112 L / α = Vas/Vb = 3.73" prints on top of the active "09 Loudspeaker" rail pill and the turntable's plinth leg, and "EXCURSION · 96 dB / ±4.22 mm at 40 Hz" is drawn over the red band of another graph.
findings.fix: In src/stages/speaker.js separate the two top anchors by at least 0.30 m in world X and give the second an offset[1] of -34. Move SEALED CHAMBER to the cabinet's right side (offset [+80, 0]). Move EXCURSION off the red band onto the card's dark margin.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: A large unlabelled white arrow at device x 820-1050, y 520-570 points left at nothing, and a long amber arc runs from device x 680 to x 2240 across empty floor at the bottom of frame with no label and no visible endpoint. Both read as leftover construction geometry.

findings.what: Two labels are cut by the hardware: "INNER GROOVE · 60.3 MM / λ at 10 kHz = 21 µm / 0.211 m/s" has its kicker broken by the dust-cover hinge, and "STYLUS ... / r 109.0 mm · 0.380 m/s" is bisected by the tonearm pillar and cueing lever. This is the depth-test bug manifesting — the labels sit in front of geometry they should be behind, or behind geometry they should clear.

findings.what: A large detail-free black slab occupies device x 530-1260, y 905-1195 behind the platter — presumably the dust cover raised, but with no edge highlight, no glass reflection and no visible hinge it reads as an unexplained floating cube and eats the frame's upper-left quadrant. Meanwhile a bright sliver of the right loudspeaker is squeezed into the 30 px between the plinth and the panel at device x 2200-2260.
findings.fix: Give the dust cover the clearGlass material with a visible edge fillet and one soft-box reflection so it reads as a lid, or remove it from this shot. Nudge SHOT at turntable.js:616 to target.x -2.32 (from -2.200) so the right-hand speaker sliver falls fully outside the SAFE box rather than half in it.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: Focal length and distance are not being matched to subject size — the contract's own example. The 92 mm DAC (dac.js:557, fov 33), the whole 1.13 m rack (preamp.js:686, fov 32; phono.js:681, fov 34; xover.js:562, fov 33) and the 1.25 m loudspeaker (speaker.js:754, fov 36) are all shot at essentially the same 31-36° field. A small object shot at the same angle as a large one reads as a toy: no compression, no separation from the background.
findings.fix: Set focal length by subject height. Rack-bay components (0.09-0.16 m tall): fov 20-24 from further back — this is the equivalent of a 100-135 mm lens and is what gives a Devialet slab its machined-solid read. The floorstander and the monoblock: fov 28-32. Room-scale (overview, sub, air): fov 34-40. Right now everything is at the middle setting and nothing gets the right treatment.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: The crossover's rear panel renders as a detached slab hovering in mid-air at device x 590-1320, y 680-880, above and to the left of the rack, with no visible connection to any chassis. It reads as a bug, not a cutaway. Its label "REAR · 2 IN, 6 OUT / 6 amplifier channels" sits hard against the left frame edge with a leader crossing the chapter rail.
findings.fix: In src/stages/xover.js, either tether the rear panel to the crossover chassis with a visible ghosted extrusion (a translucent volume connecting it back to bay 5) so it reads as an exploded view, or move it flush against the rack's rear plane. Move its label to the panel's right side, offset [+90, 0], clear of x < 320.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: The diagram card's right edge sits about 15 px from the explanation panel's left edge — zero gutter. Nothing is technically clipped, but two hard vertical edges 15 px apart create a visual seam that reads as a layout accident. The same tightness appears in phono (PCB card ~20 px from the panel) and dac (right graph column running to the panel edge).
findings.fix: Enforce a minimum 80 px gutter between any overlay geometry's projected bounding box and device x = 2280. In practice: shrink or shift each of those three cards' world-space width by roughly 12%.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: Chromatic aberration is set too strong for the subject matter. src/core/renderer.js:22 has uCA = 0.0011 and the shader applies off = c * uCA * r2 * 4.0, giving roughly 4 device px (about 2 CSS px) of R/B separation at the frame corners. On thin high-contrast geometry — the chair's chrome sled in overview, the monoblock's corner posts in amp, the turntable plinth legs in speaker — it reads as a colour bug rather than a lens characteristic. A high-end product shot has visibly less than a pixel of lateral CA at the corner.
findings.fix: Halve uCA to about 0.0005, and optionally gate it on local contrast so it only appears on genuinely blown highlights. This is a core file — report rather than patch.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: The amber mains loop in front of the rack (device x 500-1600, y 1150-1300) is a tangle of doubled-back squiggles that reads as spaghetti rather than a cable, and the cyan signal path makes a decorative serpentine bracket to the left of the rack that carries no information. Between them they are the busiest thing in the lower-middle of the opening spread, competing with the hardware they are supposed to connect.
findings.fix: Simplify both to a single clean run each, with the loop closure shown as one visible return leg rather than four folds. In an opening spread the paths should be readable at a glance as "mains in, signal through, acoustic out" — three gestures, not thirty.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: The "MAINS LEAD / 3 × 2.5 mm² · ⌀14.0 mm · 2.0 m" label floats in a black void at device x 500-780, y 1500-1560, attached to a cable that renders as thin outlined tubes with visible gaps — it reads as wireframe, not as a flexible cable. The whole bottom 20% of the frame is otherwise empty floor.
findings.fix: Either give the mains lead a real DIAG.tube with the rubber material and a contact shadow where it meets the floor, or cut it and the label. Then raise the camera target so the empty floor band is reduced to about 10% of frame height.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: Negative space is distributed as dead bands rather than as an editorial rest. overview has ~18% pure black across the top and ~20% empty floor at the bottom while the hardware is squeezed into a 27%-tall middle band. power has ~25% dead top and ~20% dead bottom. preamp has an empty top strip across device x 400-2260, y 0-300 and an empty grey patch at device x 1320-1690, y 1320-2000. In each case the emptiness is in the wrong place: it is above and below the subject rather than beside it, which is what makes a spread breathe.
findings.fix: Reframe so the subject occupies 55-70% of the SAFE box height and the rest is concentrated on one side — the classic arrangement is subject left-of-centre, rest to the right leading into the panel. Raise camera targets by 0.10-0.18 m across overview, power and preamp to lift the subject into the upper two-thirds and eliminate the top band.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: The label "ANALOGUE | DIGITAL / screened clock, split ground" prints across a shelf front whose chrome highlight runs straight through the middle of the text — the word ANALOGUE is bisected by the highlight and effectively unreadable at full resolution.
findings.fix: Move the anchor down and left onto the dark shelf underside with offset [-40, +22], or suppress it once the depth test lands. Any label whose projected position lands on a specular streak needs to move; this is the most visible instance.
findings.lens: Composition, framing and staging

findings.what: The studio environment has no front hemisphere. In /Users/richardshaer/HiFi Vis/src/core/env.js the emitters are key (9x6, intensity 5.4, at z=+3.4 but aimed back at origin), strip (16x0.62, 13.0, z=-4.6), strip2 (7.5x0.42, 9.0, x=+6.4) and kick (2.6x1.4, 2.4, x=+4.4 z=-2.4) — all above, behind or beside. The only forward source is `fill` (12x5) at intensity 0.62. Every surface facing camera therefore integrates a near-black hemisphere. This is why M.alu fascias (color 0xb9bcc0, metalness 1.0) render at ~10% grey and read as dark plastic — dac.js line 416 even pushes envMapIntensity to 1.55 and it still comes out black — and why pianoBlack cabinets are flat cards. I verified by patching scene.environmentIntensity from 1.15 to 3.0 at runtime: top faces lift, fascias barely move.
findings.fix: In src/core/env.js raise `fill` from 0.62 to 3.2 and enlarge it to panel(16, 8, 0xcfe0f6, 3.2) at (1.0, 2.6, 8.0) still lookAt(0,1.0,0). Add a second forward source: a tall narrow camera-left bounce card, panel(1.1, 5.5, 0xf2f6ff, 7.0) at (-3.4, 2.6, 4.2) lookAt(0,1.0,0) — that is the source that draws the long unbroken vertical reflection down a Wilson cabinet, and nothing in the current rig can produce one. Also lift the shell() gradient in the same file: ceil 0.018->0.075, horiz 0.040->0.085, floorC 0.006->0.020, so metals have a base reflected value instead of only catching one panel.
findings.lens: Materials, lighting and render quality

findings.what: Env panels are flat untextured MeshBasicMaterial, so their reflected image on any convex low-roughness surface is a hard-edged block of one value. Result: literal white SQUARES pasted on drivers. In shots/air.png at approximately (2330,1080) and (2250,1400) in original pixels there is a hard-edged white rounded square on the midrange dust cap and another on the bass cone; shots/sub.png shows four of them ringing the sub's surround at cardinal points, reading as stuck-on LEDs. They clip to 255 and then the bloom smears each into a fog halo.
findings.fix: In src/core/env.js replace the flat MeshBasicMaterial in panel() with a canvas-textured map that has a feathered border — a radial/edge falloff that reaches zero over the outer ~18% of the panel — so the reflected softbox has a soft edge like real diffusion. Keep the centre value but drop `key` from 5.4 to 3.6 and `strip` from 13.0 to 7.5 now that fill is doing work. Separately, in src/core/renderer.js line 96 drop the UnrealBloomPass from (0.42, 0.36, 0.92) to (0.22, 0.20, 0.98) so the residual clipped specular does not fog.
findings.lens: Materials, lighting and render quality

findings.what: The floor reflects nothing. mats().floor in src/core/materials.js line 180 is roughness 0.18 with clearcoat 0.85 — declared as polished — but MeshPhysicalMaterial only reflects the PMREM env, and that env's lower hemisphere is 0.006-0.009. Grepping the whole tree, there is no Reflector, no SSR, no mirrored-geometry pass anywhere. So a mirror-finish floor carries zero image of the speakers, the monoblocks, the rack or the subs. Every Wilson, McIntosh and Devialet studio shot on a dark floor shows a clean vertical mirror image; its absence is the single loudest CGI tell in the overview and sub frames.
findings.fix: Add a THREE.Reflector (three/examples/jsm/objects/Reflector.js) at y=0.0005 sized 16x14 under buildRoom() in src/core/room.js, rendered at half resolution, blended into mats().floor via a second mesh at ~0.30 opacity with a distance fade so it dies by 4 m from camera. Cheaper alternative if the draw budget will not take it: duplicate only the speaker, sub and monoblock groups with scale.y = -1, y-flipped, material opacity 0.22, depthWrite false, clipped to y<0 by a clipping plane.
findings.lens: Materials, lighting and render quality

findings.what: Diagram plates ghost the hardware. DIAG.diagramCard in /Users/richardshaer/HiFi Vis/src/core/diagram.js lines 280-290 builds its plate with opacity 0.62, depthWrite:false and renderOrder 4, so it draws over solid geometry regardless of depth AND lets 38% of it through. Visible in shots/xover.png (rack shelves and a blown post streak clearly readable through the ACOUSTIC SUM plate), shots/dac.png (the preamp's '-20' display shows through the card), shots/amp.png (whole rack ghosts through the schematic). It makes the card look like a browser overlay rather than an object in the room, and it destroys the black level the graphs need.
findings.fix: In src/core/diagram.js change the default to `opacity = 0.94` and set `mat.depthWrite = true` on the plate, keeping renderOrder for the traces only. Any stage that genuinely wants a see-through plate should pass opacity explicitly. Then re-frame power, streamer, dac, amp and xover so the card sits beside the hardware rather than in front of it, as CONTRACT.md section 4 already requires.
findings.lens: Materials, lighting and render quality

findings.what: Every edge in the scene carries an equally bright white line, including edges that face away from the key and edges that face down. In shots/phono.png the rack is effectively a neon wireframe of ~30 uniform white lines; in the 1:1 crop of shots/streamer.png the underside of a shelf has a highlight exactly as bright as its top. Cause: all env panels are THREE.DoubleSide (src/core/env.js panel(), line 22) so `key` and `strip` emit backwards as well as forwards, plus the `under` floor card at line 107. A fillet highlight that never varies along its length and never dies as the surface turns away is the classic outline-shader read, not a machined edge.
findings.fix: In src/core/env.js change panel() to THREE.FrontSide and orient each emitter deliberately (the flags at lines 90-96 must stay DoubleSide or become BackSide boxes). Drop the `under` card from 0.10 to 0.03. The goal is that a top edge is bright, a side edge is half as bright, and a bottom edge is nearly dark — that gradient along a fillet is what sells a solid object.
findings.lens: Materials, lighting and render quality

findings.what: Chromatic aberration is roughly 3.5 pixels at the frame corner — an order of magnitude more than any lens used for product work. GradeShader in /Users/richardshaer/HiFi Vis/src/core/renderer.js line 22 sets uCA 0.0011 and line 41 computes off = c * uCA * r2 * 4.0; at r2 = 0.5 that is 0.0011 in UV, i.e. ~3.5 px on a 3200-wide frame. At 1:1 it is unmistakable: the turntable strobe-dot row in shots/turntable.png and every horizontal edge highlight in shots/streamer.png carry visible red/green/magenta banding. It also fires after SMAA, so it re-introduces colour fringing that anti-aliasing has already resolved.
findings.fix: src/core/renderer.js line 22: uCA 0.0011 -> 0.00028. While in that block, line 21 uGrain 0.030 -> 0.012 (at 0.030 the grain is +/-7.6/255 and it is the only texture present across 20-50% of every frame, which is dead black floor) and line 23 uVig 0.22 -> 0.11 (22% corner falloff on a frame whose mean is already 11% kills the corners entirely).
findings.lens: Materials, lighting and render quality

findings.what: There are no contact shadows anywhere objects meet the floor or each other. Three compounding causes: (a) GEO.contactShadow (src/core/geo.js lines 240-249) paints a black blob with NormalBlending onto a floor that is already at ~6% luminance — you cannot darken black, so it does nothing; (b) key.shadow.normalBias in src/core/room.js line 198 is 0.014, i.e. 14 mm, on a scene whose smallest features are 1.5 mm bevels and 1.6 mm screws, which peter-pans every small contact; (c) key.shadow.camera spans left -8.5 to right 8.5 at mapSize 2048 (lines 190-196), giving 8.3 mm per texel, and shadow.radius 2.2 blurs that to ~2 cm, so a sharp contact darkening is not representable. In the 1:1 crop of shots/sub.png the sub box meets the floor on a hard line with no darkening at all and reads as pasted on.
findings.fix: src/core/room.js: shrink the key's shadow frustum to left/right -4.2/4.2, top/bottom 4.0/-1.0 (the equipment bounds) — that quadruples texel density to ~2 mm; set normalBias 0.014 -> 0.0025 and bias -0.00042 -> -0.00012; set shadow.radius 2.2 -> 1.2. Then raise the floor's lit value so shadows have something to remove: mats().floor color 0x121418 -> 0x1b1f25 in src/core/materials.js line 181, and lift the `pool` SpotLight (room.js line 221) from 40 to 55.
findings.lens: Materials, lighting and render quality

findings.what: The McIntosh meter reads as a decal, not glass with something glowing behind it. There IS a glass plane (src/stages/amp.js lines 474-483) but it is mats().glass cloned to opacity 0.22 with depthWrite false — on a MeshPhysicalMaterial, opacity scales the whole shaded result including the specular, so the softbox reflection that should sit in front of the graphics is at 22% strength and invisible against a dial whose brightest stop is #7fd3fb at toneMapped:false. It is also a dead-flat plane, so it catches only one narrow slice of the environment. In the 1:1 crop of shots/dac.png the meter is a pale blue rectangle with a black needle and no surface at all.
findings.fix: Split it into two meshes. Keep the 0.22 smoke tint as-is, then add a second plane 0.4 mm in front with MeshPhysicalMaterial({ color:0x000000, metalness:0, roughness:0.02, envMapIntensity:2.6, transparent:true, opacity:1, blending:THREE.AdditiveBlending, depthWrite:false }) — an env-only specular layer that adds a reflection on top of the glow instead of multiplying it down. Give it a 2.5 degree tilt about X, or build it as a very shallow cylindrical section (sag ~0.4 mm), so a strip highlight sweeps across the face rather than missing it entirely.
findings.lens: Materials, lighting and render quality

findings.what: The meter blue is a washed-out lightbox, not McIntosh cobalt. dialTexture() in src/stages/amp.js lines 245-249 runs the radial gradient #7fd3fb -> #41abe6 -> #1f7cba -> #12558c with the hotspot at the bottom, drawn toneMapped:false, so most of the meter face sits above 80% luminance and near-white. Real MC1.25KW/MC275 meter glass is a deep cyan-leaning cobalt with a modest lamp lift and crisp black silkscreen; the reference blooms only slightly. Here the face outshines the chassis and the ticks and 'POWER OUTPUT' legend are illegible mush even at 3200 px.
findings.fix: src/stages/amp.js lines 245-249: change the stops to #4fb6ee / #2f8ecb / #17629c / #0d4272. Raise the ink alpha from 0.95/0.62 to 1.0/0.80 and lineWidth 6.5/2.6 to 8/3.5 so the ticks survive the mip chain; set the dial texture's anisotropy to renderer.capabilities.getMaxAnisotropy() and generateMipmaps true. Same treatment for the identical pale-blue meters visible in preamp.png, dac.png and speaker.png.
findings.lens: Materials, lighting and render quality

findings.what: The motor cutaway is untextured grey and pale-blue boxes with a giant blotchy noise pattern across the magnet — exactly the 'grey plastic box' the contract bans, and the worst-looking material in the piece. In buildSection() (src/stages/speaker.js lines 596-620) `st` and `mg` are clones of steel and lamination, both of which carry roughnessMap = anodisedRough(512). The parts are built with slab()/ExtrudeGeometry, whose WorldUVGenerator emits UVs in metres, so a 0.021 m ring magnet samples about 2% of a 512 px noise texture — a single blotch magnified ~50x. That is the mottled cloud on the top magnet block in shots/speaker.png.
findings.fix: In src/stages/speaker.js buildSection(): set st.roughnessMap = null and mg.roughnessMap = null (and normalMap = null on any anodised clone used on slab geometry), or clone the texture and set .repeat.set(40,40) with wrapS/wrapT = RepeatWrapping. Then give the section real material separation: mg (ferrite) color 0x2e3238 roughness 0.72 metalness 0.35; st (pole and plates, machined low-carbon steel) color 0x8d949d roughness 0.30 metalness 1.0 with a 0.6 mm bevel on the gap corners so the top plate gets an edge highlight. Right now nothing in the motor has a broken edge and every corner is razor-sharp.
findings.lens: Materials, lighting and render quality

findings.what: The record is dead matte black with no groove sheen and no label. mats().vinyl (src/core/materials.js line 173) is roughness 0.20, vinylGrooves roughnessMap, clearcoat 0.5 — it should throw a bright concentric anisotropic arc across the disc, which is the single most recognisable specular behaviour of a record under studio light. In the 1:1 crop it is a featureless black disk; the tonearm above it casts no visible reflection into it either, and the gloss plinth top under the platter is equally dead. The platter rim, by contrast, produces the best specular arc in the entire twelve-frame set, which proves the rig can do it — the disc surface just is not catching anything.
findings.fix: Two changes. In src/core/materials.js give M.vinyl anisotropy 0.85 with anisotropyRotation driven per-fragment is not available, so instead build the record disc as a LatheGeometry (not a plane/circle) with ~256 radial segments and radial UVs so the roughnessMap runs circumferentially, and set clearcoatRoughness 0.06, envMapIntensity 1.4. Then in src/stages/turntable.js add a printed label texture (a plain dark-amber annulus with fine concentric ruling is enough) — a record with no label reads as a rubber mat. This fix depends on finding 1 landing: with a proper camera-left bounce card there will finally be something for the disc to reflect.
findings.lens: Materials, lighting and render quality

findings.what: Global exposure is far below product-render level. Measured over the 3D region (left 2280 px) of all twelve shots, mean luminance is 8.8-14.5% of full scale, with 20-54% of the pixel area below 5% and, in streamer, 44% below 2%. Peak specular occupies 0.002-0.03% of the frame. A McIntosh or Wilson press shot sits nearer 25-40% mean with a full black point and a specular that just kisses 100% across maybe 0.5% of area. The consequence is that the piece has almost no midtones: it is black, plus thin white lines, plus cyan UI. There is no tonal range in which a material can be read.
findings.fix: After landing findings 1 and 5, raise renderer.toneMappingExposure in src/core/renderer.js line 75 from 1.30 to about 1.55 and re-measure. Target: mean 22-28% over the 3D region and under 15% of area below 5%. Also lift the backdrop: seamlessBackdrop() in src/core/room.js line 60 is color 0x14161a envMapIntensity 0.7 — take it to 0x1e2127 / 0.95 so the cyclorama holds a readable gradient instead of falling to the same value as the floor.
findings.lens: Materials, lighting and render quality

findings.what: Gloss lacquer has no clearcoat depth — there is a specular term and a diffuse term but they never separate. mats().pianoBlack (src/core/materials.js lines 92-96) is correctly built (color 0x08090b, clearcoat 1.0, clearcoatRoughness 0.028) yet every cabinet in overview.png, speaker.png, sub.png and air.png renders as a single flat value per face with no gradient from top to bottom. On a real Wilson cabinet the side cheek runs dark at the top (ceiling flag), through a bright band where the strip light lands, to dark again at the plinth — and that vertical gradient is most of what says 'automotive lacquer'. It is absent because the environment has no vertical structure for the clearcoat to reflect.
findings.fix: Falls out of finding 1 plus one addition: in src/core/env.js the shell() fragment shader currently produces three smooth bands. Add visible structure — a brighter horizon band around y=0.02..0.12 at roughly 0.11, and two dim vertical dark strips (light-stand flags) at azimuth +/-40 degrees — so a mirror surface reflects a broken scene rather than a single value. Verify by looking at the speaker cheek in shots/overview.png: it must show a top-to-bottom value change of at least 3:1 after the fix.
findings.lens: Materials, lighting and render quality

findings.what: A flat desaturated teal wash covers the entire lower half of shots/sub.png, terminating in a hard straight seam across the full frame width at roughly y=1150 (original px). It sits over the polished floor and over the listening chair, raising the black level of the largest single area in the frame to a muddy mid-teal with no gradient and no depth cue. It is exactly the scene-wide haze CONTRACT.md section 3 warns about, and it also swamps the accent-colour discipline (rule 5) by making teal the dominant hue of the composition.
findings.fix: In src/stages/sub.js reduce the modal-pressure plane's opacity to about 0.30 of its current value, replace its hard rectangular boundary with a radial alpha falloff to zero at the edges (a canvas mask, same approach as blobShadow), and change its blending from additive to NormalBlending with a colour that stays under the floor's own value so it reads as a projection onto the floor rather than a light in the room. Keep the node/antinode contrast by raising the *modulation* depth rather than the base level.
findings.lens: Materials, lighting and render quality

findings.what: The stage named Monoblocks does not show a monoblock. In shots/amp.png the camera frames the rack; the monoblock is at the extreme left edge, cropped by the frame, unlit, and behind the chapter rail, while a 62%-opaque schematic covers the rack. From a materials standpoint this is fatal — the piece's most McIntosh-like object (fascia, meter, ribs, heatsink, binding posts, all of which amp.js actually builds in detail at lines 390-500) is never presented. Separately the heatsink fins in every frame that shows one (dac.png, air.png) are a solid black void: GEO.heatsink builds real fins but no light reaches into the valleys and no fin tip carries an edge highlight.
findings.fix: Re-shoot the amp stage from the monoblock: put shot.position roughly 3/4-front-left of LAYOUT.monoR at 0.9-1.1 m out and 0.55 m high with fov 30, and move the schematic card to camera-right beside it. For the fins, add a small forward-right emitter in src/core/env.js — panel(1.6, 1.2, 0xe8eef8, 4.0) at (2.6, 1.1, 2.2) lookAt(0.6, 0.6, -1.0) — aimed to rake across the fin stack, and give the fin geometry in src/core/geo.js line 96 a larger bevel (0.0006 -> 0.0011) so each tip can hold a line.
findings.lens: Materials, lighting and render quality

findings.what: The bass drivers are unresolved at hero scale. In the 1:1 crop of shots/speaker.png each woofer is a flat black dish inside a chrome-ish ring: no cast-basket spokes, no spider, no visible fasteners, no dust-cap separation, and the rubber roll surround catches a hard square instead of the crisp arc a real surround shows. GEO.driverBasket exists in src/core/geo.js line 296 and is not being used here, and mats().cone (roughness 0.88, sheen 0.55) gives no fibre texture at all.
findings.fix: In src/stages/speaker.js makeDriver(), add GEO.driverBasket behind each cone and a ring of GEO.screw at the flange (8 for the woofers, 6 for the mid) — CONTRACT.md rule 3 asks for exactly this and it is what sells the scale. Give mats().cone a fine radial normal map or at minimum drop roughness to 0.74 and raise sheenColor to 0x454b55 so the cone shows a value change from rim to apex. The hard square on the surround resolves with finding 2.
findings.lens: Materials, lighting and render quality

findings.what: Knobs render as flat discs with a four-quadrant pinwheel gradient and no visible knurling. Clear at 1:1 in shots/streamer.png (the large knob at roughly x=890,y=240 in the crop) and shots/dac.png. GEO.knob (src/core/geo.js lines 62-86) does build 56 instanced flutes at 0.7 mm x 1.6 mm, but at the shot distances those are sub-pixel and average into mush, while the 64-segment bevelCyl body shows visible facet banding under the envmap.
findings.fix: In src/core/geo.js raise the knob body's radial segments from 64 to 96 and the bevel from 0.0009 to 0.0014 so the top chamfer holds a continuous ring highlight; increase flute cross-section to 0.0011 x 0.0022 and drop the count from 56 to 40 so each flute is at least a pixel wide at the stage framing. Add a chrome collar ring at the knob base (bevelCyl at r*1.06, 1.2 mm tall, mats().chrome) — that ring is what actually reads as a machined control at this distance.
findings.lens: Materials, lighting and render quality

findings.what: The cartridge — the subject of this stage's physics — is an unresolved dark box with a white blob, and the tonearm bearing yoke carries a hard-clipped white rectangle at roughly (740,250) in the 1:1 crop. Meanwhile the platter-edge knurl aliases into a shimmering dashed pattern, and there is no darkening where the platter rim meets the plinth or where the arm pillar meets it, so both float.
